elements.evidence: The rendered clause retains an operative non-solicit that binds Customer (Licensee): "neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party who is directly involved in performing services under this Agreement". A restriction on Customer therefore survives; the preferred position (deletion of any Customer-side non-solicit) is not achieved.

Operative text changed from "the Licensee will not solicit any person employed by Licensor and/or its Affiliates" to "neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party ... to leave his or her employment with that party", which binds both parties symmetrically.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Scope is limited to "any person employed by the other party who is directly involved in performing services under this Agreement", replacing the prior all-employees-and-Affiliates scope.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "during the twelve (12) month period after the end of a person's involvement in services under this Agreement" — 12 months anchored to the end of involvement, exactly the fallback temporal anchor. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a matcher artefact; the numeral "twelve (12)" is present in the rendered operative sentence.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Retained definition: "the term \"Solicit\" ... shall not mean generally advertising job openings".

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Retained definition excludes "activities that constitute follow-up to individuals who respond to job opening advertisements or who voluntarily initiate employment inquiries."

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The only prohibited act is to "solicit ... to leave his or her employment", and "Solicit" is defined as "any affirmative recruitment specifically aimed at one or more individuals identified by name, title or affiliation". There is no "employ or engage" or no-hire language anywhere in the clause.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: all six atomic elements are met on the face of the rendered operative language (three cured by the edit, three already met by the retained "Solicit" definition).

Preferred level is not met and was not targeted: a mutual non-solicit still binds Customer. That is acceptable because the claimed target is the fallback, and a clause at the fallback is a defensible landing point.

Minimality holds. Three edits map one-to-one to the three unmet elements: party direction ("neither party ... the other party"), scope ("directly involved in performing services under this Agreement") and duration/anchor ("twelve (12) month period after the end of a person's involvement"). Dropping "and/or its Affiliates" is a direct consequence of the mutual "employed by the other party" formulation rather than a free-standing extra. No survival tail, expense language, procedure or boilerplate was added, and the favourable existing carve-out sentence was retained verbatim.

Intent is preserved. The clause heading "NON SOLICITATION" and Article X(b) numbering survive, so the Article XI injunctive-relief cross-reference to the non-solicitation covenant still resolves; the reference merely describes a covenant that is now reciprocal, which is not a contradiction of retained operative text. No term is left undefined and the "Solicit" definition continues to operate on the amended sentence.

Note for the drafter (no repair required): the deterministic duration check flagged "number not found", but substantive inspection confirms "twelve (12) month period" in the operative sentence; if the pipeline gate is blocking, align the regex rather than the language.

Optional polish, not a defect: Article XI's descriptive phrase "Non Solicitation of Licensor Employees" now understates a mutual covenant. If the counterparty raises it, conform that descriptor to "Non Solicitation" — but leaving it is preferable to a broader edit and does not create a dangling reference.
